match.reason: The closest bank point, Land biomes, teaches the global pattern of biome bands rather than where Australia's biomes sit, and it does not cover shrubland, so the Australian point would need new content and not a small adjustment.

draft.title: Australia's biomes
card: Australia has many biomes because it is large and its climate changes from place to place. Rainfall and temperature differ between the north, the inland and the south.
The north has tropical rainforest and savanna. These are the warmest parts of the country, and they get most of their rain in a wet season.
The inland has desert and shrubland. This is the driest part of Australia, with low and unreliable rainfall.
The south-east and south-west have temperate forest and grassland. These areas are cooler than the north and have milder, more regular rain.
draft.remember: Australia's biomes change with climate: tropical in the north, dry inland, temperate in the south.

a.q: Which pair of biomes is found mainly in northern Australia?
a.why: The warm north, with a wet season, has tropical rainforest and savanna. Desert and shrubland are tempting, but they are found in the dry inland, not the north.
a.clue: Think of the warmest part of the country, with a wet season.

b.q: Priya drives from Melbourne to the middle of Australia. Her trip passes from the temperate south-east into dry country with low, unreliable rain. Which biomes does she most likely see in the dry country?
b.why: Low and unreliable rainfall in the inland suits desert and shrubland. Temperate forest and grassland are tempting because she starts in the south-east, but those biomes have milder, more regular rain.
b.clue: Which part of Australia is the driest?

wants.brief: A map of Australia showing its main biomes as coloured regions: tropical rainforest and savanna in the north, desert and shrubland inland, temperate forest and grassland in the south-east and south-west, each with a legend label.
wants.why: Students see where each biome lies across the country.
